entities.summary:
Socrates Chrestus, a second son of Nicomedes III of Bithynia, usurped the throne by deposing his brother Nicomedes IV, marking a pivotal moment in Bithynian history. This event had significant repercussions in the region, influencing the power dynamics of the Hellenistic world. The consequences of Socrates' actions can be seen in the subsequent history of Bithynia and its interactions with neighboring powers.

Socrates' reign was marked by a series of challenges and opportunities, including the rise of the Roman Empire and the ongoing struggles of the Hellenistic kingdoms.

The legacy of Socrates Chrestus extends beyond his own dynasty, with his actions contributing to the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the ancient world.

The intricate dance of power and politics that Socrates Chrestus played was set against the backdrop of a rapidly changing world, with the Roman Empire's expansion and the rise of new cultural and religious movements shaping the course of human history.
